findings.claim: Hook containment and policy-approved root whitelist behavior is unspecified, so execute would invent the security model.
findings.analysis: The change edits literal-branch approval, svc-ensure-worktree containment, and multiple worktree detectors on session/tool/install paths. The plan only says roots will be dynamically whitelisted from ~/.svc/worktree-policy.json while keeping UID and symlink checks, and that a containment anchor will be passed through creation/resume. It does not bind schema fields, which paths may become approved roots, whether a same-UID writable policy can add arbitrary directories, how UID/symlink checks compose with the whitelist, what the containment anchor value is at each call site, or deny behavior when a candidate is outside approved roots. Treating absent and unparseable policy identically as graceful default-to-standard-layout is fail-open for a security-relevant config and can expand or redirect approved roots without an operator intent signal.
evidence: Implementation Summary: 'dynamically whitelist policy-approved roots while maintaining strict UID and symlink checks.'
Implementation Summary: 'dynamically pass containment anchor through worktree creation, fresh setup, and forward completion.'
External State: 'If policy is absent or unparseable, resolver defaults gracefully to standard layout.'
External State names ~/.svc/worktree-policy.json mode 0600 with no field list, allowlist rule, or deny matrix.
No planning_contract/implementation_approach function or CLI contract for worktree-policy.mjs, literal-branch.mjs, or svc-ensure-worktree.mjs.
findings.proposed_fix: Seal a security contract before execute: schema fields and defaults for worktree-policy.json; exact approved-root algorithm; deny vs default matrix for missing, unreadable, schema-invalid, symlink, cross-UID, and out-of-root cases (defaults only for intentional absence); concrete containment-anchor value and every svc-ensure-worktree call site; negative proofs that symlink ancestors, foreign UID, and paths outside approved roots fail closed.

findings.claim: There is no commit-scoped rollback path, and installer/policy rerun semantics after partial execute are unbound.
findings.analysis: Dimension (c) requires a concrete revert of implementing commits. 'Rollback Safety' is a runtime fallback when policy is absent/unparseable, which does not restore a known tree and does not undo ~/worktrees, policy.json, gitdir links, or already-deployed hook behavior. Idempotency is unspecified for preexisting ~/worktrees with wrong mode, preexisting policy with extra roots, task-1 landed while task-2 failed, or mixed hook/CLI roots after partial execute. Parallel task-3/task-2 after task-1 can leave new resolvers live without the security patch.
evidence: External State Rollback Safety: 'If policy is absent or unparseable, resolver defaults gracefully to standard layout.'
No git revert / worktree cleanup sequence scoped to the feature commit.
task-4 initializes directory and policy with no exists-wrong-mode or partial-rerun rule.
task-3 and task-2 both depend only on task-1 and can diverge if one fails.
findings.proposed_fix: Add recovery: revert implementation commit(s); list then remove only WI-created worktrees under the sealed layout; leave pre-existing user policy/dirs untouched unless created by this WI (record paths in the exec receipt). Specify setup rerun refuse/overwrite rules and a sequential cutover so resolvers and callers cannot diverge mid-execute.
